subject: FinTechCo discovery — follow-up: token volumes, budget, and EU data residency
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Hoffman <lena@fintechco.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: FinTechCo discovery — follow-up: token volumes, budget, and EU data residency

Hi Lena — thanks again for a great discovery call earlier. Quick recap and a couple of follow-ups so we can model pricing for the use cases you described.

Recap (from our notes):
- Primary use case: real-time fraud detection + summarized explanations to analysts (short responses ~40–80 tok).
- Secondary use case: nightly batch re-rerank of historical events (longer contexts, up to ~2k toks in some cases).
- Expected concurrency: small number of high-QPS endpoints during market hours (peaks ~120 requests/sec across service).
- Data residency: EU customer data must remain in EU for regulated flows; some non-PII telemetry can live in US.

Follow-ups we need to finalize pricing modeling:
1) Monthly token volumes by workload (real-time vs batch). Ballpark is fine — helps choose model size/quantization and batching assumptions.
2) Target unit economics: you mentioned wanting to budget ~$X per 1M tokens — can you confirm the target $/1M token range?
3) Residency split: what % of requests need EU-only hosting vs US-allowed?
4) Sequence length distribution for the real-time flow (p50/p90) and batch average.
5) Any specific SLA or dedicated capacity needs for market hours?

Preliminary note on regional cost: serving from EU regions typically adds ~10–25% to unit cost versus US (depends on reserved capacity vs shared hosted, and whether we need a dedicated EU-only pool). If you need strict EU-only VPC/private deployment that also increases fixed monthly costs (reserved capacity/replicas).

Attached a simple token-profile workbook (FinTechCo_Token_Profile.xlsx) and our draft US/EU price reference (Redwood_pricing_us-eu_v1.pdf) — I filled in a few sample scenarios.

If you can send the ballpark numbers for items 1–3 above, Ben and Neha and I will run two scenarios (hosted vs dedicated EU pool) and send a short ROI table tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: FinTechCo_Token_Profile.xlsx (spreadsheet, token estimates); Redwood_pricing_us-eu_v1.pdf (pricing assumptions)

From: Lena Hoffman <lena@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinTechCo Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 23:10:00 +0100
Subject: Re: FinTechCo discovery — follow-up: token volumes, budget, and EU data residency

Hi Marissa — thanks for the recap and the attachments. Confirming ballpark numbers so you can run scenarios:

1) Monthly volumes (estimates):
- Real-time fraud detection: 250M–400M tokens/month (mostly short responses, p50 ~60 toks, p90 ~140 toks).
- Nightly batch re-rank: 150M–250M tokens/month (avg ~800–1,200 toks per item).
- Total: 400M–650M tokens/month.

2) Budget / target unit economics:
- Our initial procurement target is $700–$1,000 per 1M tokens USD (this is for budgeting; we understand discounts for committed volume).

3) Residency split:
- Regulated flows (account data + protected transaction telemetry) must stay in EU: ~65% of requests by token volume.
- Remaining 35% can be hosted in US or multi-region.

4) SLA: We need <200ms p95 latency for the real-time inference path during market hours; happy to consider dedicated capacity if that’s the only reliable way.

We also have a procurement questionnaire coming through — procurement@fintechco.com will follow up with contract and security questions.

Thanks,
Lena Hoffman
Head of ML Platform — FinTechCo
Lena.Hoffman@fintechco.com

Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinTechCo discovery — follow-up: token volumes, budget, and EU data residency

Thanks Marissa and Lena — good data, this helps a lot. I ran back-of-envelope scenarios with Neha and attached an updated pricing note (see Redwood_pricing_us-eu_v1.pdf, v2 tab). High-level calls:

1) Unit economics (hosted estimate, US region): with 500M tokens/month mixed (real-time + batch) and typical batching, we land around ~$850 per 1M tokens USD.
2) EU region delta: for strict EU-only hosting (hosted multi-tenant) expect ~+15% on unit cost (~$980 per 1M tokens). If they require dedicated EU reserved capacity (to meet the <200ms p95 SLA) there’s a fixed-cost component — net unit cost depends on commit level, but a conservative blended estimate is ~$1,100–$1,250 per 1M tokens.
3) Discount levers: committed monthly volume (12–24mo), prewarming for market hours, and optimized quantization for batch workloads all reduce effective $/1M. Neha: we should run a scenario with 12mo commit at 500M/mo and with mixed quantization — please drop numbers in the workbook.

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa: send the updated workbook to Lena and procurement with a 2-sheet deliverable (hosted US primary, hosted EU dedicated) plus a short notes page explaining the EU fixed cost drivers.
- Neha: populate the 12mo commit row + dedicated EU reserved pool estimate in the workbook.
- Marissa/Ben: schedule a 30-min pricing review with Lena + procurement next week.

Lena — any preference for meeting cadence? We can do a one-off walkthrough or walk procurement through the workbook live (DocuSign/contract timeline tends to go faster if procurement sees a concrete committed-price scenario).

Ben Carter

ben@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0199
